concepts.title: Flux Linking a Tilted Coil
concepts.definition: The field-catch of a loop equals the field strength times its area times the cosine of the angle between the field and the area normal; for patchy fields the patch contributions are summed, and the weber is the unit.
concepts.key_idea: Any of the three factors - field, area, orientation - can be varied to create the flux change that drives induction.

concepts.title: Induced Emf from Faraday Law
concepts.definition: A coil develops an emf whenever the flux threading it changes, with size equal to the turn count times how fast the flux changes per second; the minus sign only carries direction information.
concepts.key_idea: Steady flux gives no emf no matter how strong the field; only the rate of change matters, so faster motion or quicker switching yields larger emf.

concepts.title: Induced Current in a Closed Loop
concepts.definition: Once a loop offers resistance R, the induced emf drives a current of emf over R through it, and that current is what a galvanometer actually registers.
concepts.key_idea: Same emf, smaller resistance, bigger current; the emf itself appears even in an open circuit with no current at all.

concepts.title: Lenz Law Direction Rule
concepts.definition: The induced current always picks the sense that fights the flux change causing it - pushing back on an approaching magnet and grabbing a departing one - which is exactly what energy conservation demands.
concepts.formula: induced effect opposes the flux change that made it
concepts.key_idea: The work you do against the opposing push becomes the Joule heat of the induced current, so a perpetual-motion shortcut is impossible.

concepts.title: Emf of a Rotating Conductor
concepts.definition: Spin a rod about one end in an axial field and each slice dr of the rod contributes B v dr; integrating with v = omega r gives a centre-to-tip emf of half B omega R squared.
concepts.key_idea: Spokes act in parallel, so a wheel with many spokes gives the same emf as one rod; only the rim speed profile matters.

concepts.title: Inductance as Flux Linkage per Current
concepts.definition: For any fixed coil geometry the flux linkage N phi runs proportional to the current that makes it, and the ratio defines the inductance, a geometry-only scalar measured in henry.
concepts.key_idea: Inductance is the electromagnetic cousin of capacitance: set by shape and core material, not by how much current flows.

concepts.title: Mutual Inductance Between Two Coils
concepts.definition: A current changing in one coil at rate dI/dt drops an emf of M times that rate in its neighbour; the pairing constant M is symmetric (M12 = M21) and for coaxial solenoids equals mu0 n1 n2 pi r1 squared l.
concepts.key_idea: Symmetry of M lets you compute the easy direction: a small inner coil inside a big one feels a uniform field, so M follows at once.

concepts.title: Self Inductance and the Back Emf
concepts.definition: A coil fighting its own current change generates a back emf of L dI/dt opposite to the change, acting like electrical inertia against both growth and decay of current.
concepts.key_idea: Estimate L from a measured shutdown: L equals the average emf times the decay time over the current dropped.

concepts.title: Solenoid Self Inductance
concepts.definition: For a long solenoid the linkage works out to mu0 n squared A l times the current, so its inductance is mu0 n squared A l - and an iron core of relative permeability mur multiplies that again.
concepts.formula: sol_ind = mu_0 * perm_rel * turns_per_len ** 2 * area * solenoid_len
concepts.key_idea: Inductance grows with the square of the turn density, so winding more turns into the same length is the fastest way to raise L.

concepts.title: Energy Stored in an Inductor
concepts.definition: Building a current against the back emf banks work in the coil's field; the store equals half L I squared, the exact analogue of kinetic energy with L standing in for mass.
concepts.key_idea: The work rate is emf times current; integrating L I dI/dt over the buildup collects half L I squared in the magnetic field.

concepts.title: Magnetic Energy Density in a Field
concepts.definition: Dividing an inductor's stored energy by its volume leaves B squared over 2 mu0 per unit volume - a universal price tag for magnetic field, matching epsilon0 E squared over 2 on the electric side.
concepts.key_idea: Energy lives in the field itself, not the wires: any region holding field B carries this density, whether or not a coil is around.

concepts.title: Peak Emf of an AC Generator
concepts.definition: Rotating a coil at constant rate makes its flux swing as BA cos(omega t), so the emf alternates sinusoidally with peak value NBA omega, delivered to the circuit through slip rings and brushes.
concepts.key_idea: Mechanical rotation becomes alternating electricity; the extrema land where the flux changes fastest, at coil edges parallel to the field.
